name: @dudo/contracts
description: The published contract set. This PACKAGE exports only the generated TypeScript types (ADR 0037); the YAML, the schemas, the generator and the validators are not importable.
//: WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL, AND WHY IT IS A PACKAGE RATHER THAN AN ALIAS.
0037 requires that generated types be CONSUMED and never re-declared. Until
2026-09-09 no consumer could import one: this directory was not a workspace
member and neither client carried an alias to it, so the whole point of the
generator was unreachable. web-agent measured that while blocked on it, could
have added a tsconfig path and a Vite alias inside its own boundary, and
argued against doing so. That argument is the reason for this file.
A PER-CLIENT ALIAS IS THE DIVERGENCE 0040 EXISTS TO END. Two clients and Core
consume the same contract set; three private resolutions of one shared thing
drift silently, and architecture.md §1 names a shape one client has and the
other does not as a CONTRACT DEFECT rather than a client-local workaround.
0040 already ruled the shape: shared code becomes a workspace package.
*** THE `exports` MAP IS AN ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY, NOT A CONVENIENCE. ***
It resolves `@dudo/contracts/<path>` to `./generated/<path>.ts` and exposes
NOTHING ELSE. A client cannot import the generator, the raw schemas, the YAML
or the validators — not because a rule forbids it, but because module
resolution refuses. That converts 'clients consume contracts, they do not
execute them' from a sentence in a README into a build failure, which is
architecture.md §3a's shape applied to an import graph.
AND THE IMPORT PATH MIRRORS THE CONTRACT PATH EXACTLY, which is the property
worth having:
packages/contracts/core/platform/template-v1.contract.yaml
@dudo/contracts/core/platform/template-v1
A reader holding an import knows which contract to open, and a reviewer can
check the citation without resolving anything. §3c's last variant is about a
quotation that cannot be traced to its block; this makes the trace mechanical.
IT SHIPS TypeScript SOURCE AND HAS NO BUILD, matching @dudo/ui and
@dudo/client-kdf. A build artifact here could go stale against the committed
generated output, which is the one failure mode a generated-type package must
not have.
IT HAS NO DEPENDENCIES AND NO peerDependencies. The generated modules export
TYPES ONLY — no runtime value, no import of anything. Adding this member to
the root workspaces installs nothing; it registers a symlink.
THE ROOT package.json PREVIOUSLY RECORDED THAT THIS DIRECTORY WAS DELIBERATELY
NOT A WORKSPACE — 'they are not npm packages, and adding them changes what
`npm install` does to trees that do not want it.' That was written before any
generated output existed and was correct then. It is superseded rather than
ignored: the reason it gave was a cost to other trees, and this member imposes
none, because it brings no dependency for npm to resolve.
